mainTopic: The sources that all four blood עבודות must be done לשמה, both for the right type of קרבן and for the right owner
overview: The גמרא looks for the source that every blood עבודה of a קרבן must be done לשמה. It learns שחיטה from the extra word ״זֶבַח״ in ״וְאִם זֶבַח שְׁלָמִים קׇרְבָּנוֹ״. It learns קבלה from ״הַמַּקְרִיב״ and זריקה from ״הַזּוֹרֵק״. Each עבודה has its own stringency, so none can be learned from another. הולכה is included in קבלה, because the תורה describes קבלה with a word meaning carrying. Next, רב פנחס learns that a קרבן must also be slaughtered for its owner (שינוי בעלים) from the word ״זֶבַח״ in the פסוק about the תודה. He defends this against two challenges about other lessons drawn from that פסוק. Finally, the גמרא tries to extend the owner rule to the other עבודות with a גזירה שוה from שינוי קודש. It then refutes that comparison with four ways שינוי קודש is stricter, and the search continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What is the source that slaughter must be for the right purpose?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that a קרבן's שחיטה must be done לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that the slaughtering has to be done for the sake of the קרבן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. It wants a פסוק showing that a קרבן must be slaughtered with the intention of being that specific קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know the rule that שחיטה must be לשמה. Now the גמרא wants to find exactly where the תורה teaches it. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know? (asking for a source)
Slaughtering (of a קרבן)
For its own sake, meaning with the intention of being this specific קרבן
We require

phrases.english: From where do we know that we require slaughter for its own sake?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new line of inquiry asking for the scriptural source of לשמה in שחיטה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches that שחיטה must be done לשמה.

steps.title: The source is the phrase "a sacrifice of peace offerings"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers from "וְאִם זֶבַח שְׁלָמִים קׇרְבָּנוֹ": the זביחה must be for the sake of שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: "And if his קרבן is a זֶבַח of שלמים." This teaches that the slaughter must be done for the sake of a שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source. The words "זֶבַח שְׁלָמִים" are read as "a slaughter of שלמים", meaning the slaughter must be done for the sake of שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word זֶבַח comes from the same root as זְבִיחָה (slaughtering). So the פסוק is read as connecting the act of slaughter to the name שלמים. That link is what teaches that the slaughter has to be done with שלמים in mind.

keyTerms.meaning: As the פסוק says
A sacrifice; from the same root as "slaughter"
Peace offerings
For the sake of

phrases.english: As the verse states:
"And if his offering is a sacrifice of peace offerings"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 3:1

phrases.english: that the slaughter must be for the sake of a peace offering.
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the word in square brackets. The corrected wording adds it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words "זֶבַח שְׁלָמִים" teach that the זביחה must be for the sake of שלמים.

steps.title: Maybe "זבח שלמים" is just the offering's name
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: perhaps "זֶבַח שְׁלָמִים" is simply what this קרבן is called, and teaches nothing about intention.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe that is just their name!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. Maybe the פסוק says "זֶבַח שְׁלָמִים" only because that is the full name of the קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A proof from a word only works if the word is extra. If "זֶבַח שְׁלָמִים" is just the normal name, then the word זֶבַח teaches nothing new, and the source for לשמה falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps
That is (just)
Their name

phrases.english: But perhaps that is simply their name!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the derivation given in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of "זֶבַח שְׁלָמִים" as teaching לשמה in שחיטה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If "זֶבַח שְׁלָמִים" is simply the standard name of the קרבן, the word זֶבַח is not extra and cannot teach a rule about intention.

steps.title: Other verses leave out "זבח", so here it teaches something
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that other פסוקים call the קרבן just "שלמים" without "זֶבַח". So when "זֶבַח" does appear here, it teaches that the slaughter must be for the sake of שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Other פסוקים say "who offers the blood of the שלמים" and "who sprinkles the blood of the שלמים" without the word זֶבַח. Here it does say זֶבַח. So learn from it that the slaughter must be for the sake of שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its proof. It shows that "זֶבַח" is not part of the קרבן's regular name, because other פסוקים leave it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the תורה can call this קרבן just "השלמים", the word זֶבַח in our פסוק is extra. An extra word comes to teach something, and here it teaches that the זביחה must be לשמה. This answers the challenge in step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: From the fact that it is written
The one who offers (brings near)
The one who sprinkles or throws (the blood)
Learn from it (a conclusion formula)

steps.whatToRemember: The source for לשמה in שחיטה is the word זֶבַח in "וְאִם זֶבַח שְׁלָמִים קׇרְבָּנוֹ". We know it is extra because other פסוקים call the קרבן just "השלמים".
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the proof comes just from the word שלמים. The key is the extra word זֶבַח, which shares a root with זביחה (slaughtering).

phrases.english: From the fact that it is written: "Who offers the blood of the peace offering,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:33

phrases.english: and "who sprinkles the blood of the peace offering"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:14

phrases.english: and "sacrifice" is not written there;
but here "sacrifice" is written;
learn from it:
that the slaughter must be for the sake of a peace offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 and confirms the derivation of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison with other פסוקים shows that the word is extra
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "זֶבַח שְׁלָמִים" might be just the regular name of the קרבן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Other פסוקים call it only "השלמים", so זֶבַח is extra and teaches that זביחה must be לשמה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שחיטה must be לשמה, learned from the extra word זֶבַח.

steps.title: What is the source for the other sacrificial rites?
steps.stepSummary: Having found the source for זביחה, the גמרא asks where we learn that the other עבודות must also be done לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source for slaughtering. From where do we know it for the other services?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up what it has proven and then sets up the next question. It now wants a source for the other עבודות, such as collecting, carrying, and sprinkling the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word זֶבַח only speaks about slaughtering. So the rule of לשמה for the other עבודות still needs its own source. The גמרא starts answering this in the next steps, beginning with קבלה in step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found (a source for one case)
The rest, the other
The sacrificial services (collecting, carrying, and sprinkling the blood)

phrases.english: We have found a source for slaughter;
from where do we know it for the other rites?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion of step 4 and extends the question to the other עבודות.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that קבלה, הולכה, and זריקה must also be done לשמה.

steps.title: Suggestion: learn the other עבודות from slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the other עבודות could be learned from שחיטה, which already needs to be לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: let us learn the other services from slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer to the question in Step 5. This sets up the next move, where the suggestion will be knocked down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already have a פסוק that שחיטה must be לשמה. The idea is to compare the other עבודות to שחיטה and apply the same rule to them, without needing a new פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say — introduces a suggestion the גמרא is about to answer
Let us learn (derive)
Slaughter (same as שחיטה)

phrases.english: And if you will say: let us learn from slaughter;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to the question in Step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Learn the other עבודות from שחיטה by comparison.

steps.title: Slaughter is special because of the פסח rule
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion is rejected because שחיטה has a stringency the other עבודות lack: in a קרבן פסח, slaughtering it not for the sake of its eaters makes it פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is special about slaughter? It is special because in the Paschal offering, it becomes disqualified when done not for the sake of those who will eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the suggestion from Step 6. It shows that שחיטה is stricter than the other עבודות, so we cannot copy its rules onto them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You can only learn one thing from another if they are equal. Since שחיטה has an extra stringency in the פסח that the other עבודות don't have, maybe only שחיטה needs לשמה, and the comparison fails.

keyTerms.meaning: What is special about... — a formula for pointing out a difference that breaks a comparison
Not for the sake of those who will eat it
The קרבן פסח, the Paschal offering

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying the other עבודות don't need לשמה. It only says we can't learn them from שחיטה, so we need a different source.

phrases.english: What is special about slaughter?
That it is disqualified
when done not for the sake of those who eat it, in the Paschal offering!
phrases.notes: For example, slaughtering the פסח for someone too sick to eat it makes it פסול. The other עבודות don't have this rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לִזְבִיחָה שֶׁכֵּן נִפְסְלָה שֶׁלֹּא לְשֵׁם אוֹכְלִין בַּפֶּסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison suggested in Step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning the other עבודות from שחיטה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שחיטה has a unique stringency (פסול שלא לשם אוכלין in the פסח), so it is not equal to the other עבודות.

steps.title: A separate פסוק for collecting the blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings ״הַמַּקְרִיב אֶת דַּם הַשְּׁלָמִים״ to teach that קבלה must be done for the sake of שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the verse says: 'Who offers the blood of the peace offering' — that the collection of the blood must be for the sake of a peace offering.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the comparison failed, the גמרא brings its own פסוק for קבלה. This פסוק shows that collecting the blood must also be לשמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows the earlier idea is dropped. Now קבלה has its own direct source, just like שחיטה has its own source from ״זֶבַח שְׁלָמִים״.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather — drops the previous idea and gives a new one
Collecting the animal's blood in a כלי
The one who offers

phrases.english: Rather, the verse says:
"Who offers the blood of the peace offering"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:33. Here "offering the blood" refers to the one who collects it, as the גמרא will explain.

phrases.english: that the collection must be for the sake of a peace offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר קְרָא הַמַּקְרִיב אֶת דַּם הַשְּׁלָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected comparison with a direct פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״הַמַּקְרִיב אֶת דַּם הַשְּׁלָמִים״ teaches that קבלה must be לשמה.

steps.title: Why not write it only for collection?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the Torah could have written the לשמה rule only for קבלה, and we would learn שחיטה from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the Merciful One write it only for collection, and we would learn slaughter from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges why the Torah needed two separate פסוקים. It suggests one פסוק for קבלה should be enough to teach שחיטה too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Above, learning from שחיטה failed because שחיטה is stricter. Now the גמרא tries the opposite direction: maybe learn שחיטה from קבלה, which would make the ״זֶבַח״ פסוק unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the Torah write — asks why the Torah didn't write it differently
The Merciful One — refers to ה׳, the giver of the Torah
From it

phrases.english: And let the Merciful One write it about collection,
and we would learn slaughter from it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא בְּקַבָּלָה וְלֵילַף שְׁחִיטָה מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for both the שחיטה פסוק and the קבלה פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for a separate פסוק for שחיטה (Step 2).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If קבלה has a פסוק, שחיטה could be learned from it, so the ״זֶבַח״ פסוק seems extra.

steps.title: Collection is special too: a זר or woman can't do it
steps.stepSummary: We can't learn שחיטה from קבלה, because קבלה is stricter: it is פסול when done by a זר or a woman, while שחיטה is valid by them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because one can refute it: what is special about collection? It is invalid when done by a non-כהן or a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in Step 9. Each עבודה has its own stringency, so neither can be learned from the other, and both פסוקים are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קבלה must be done by a כהן, but שחיטה can be done by anyone, even a זר or a woman. Since קבלה is stricter in this way, maybe only it needs לשמה, so שחיטה needs its own פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: One can refute it — there is a difference that breaks the comparison
A non-כהן
Invalid

steps.whatToRemember: שחיטה and קבלה each need their own פסוק for לשמה. שחיטה is stricter in the פסח, and קבלה is stricter because it needs a כהן, so neither can be learned from the other.

phrases.english: Because one can refute it:
What is special about collection?
That it is invalid by a non-priest or a woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: פירכא — showing the source case has a stringency the other case lacks
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שחיטה could be learned from קבלה, so one פסוק would be enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: קבלה is stricter (פסול בזר ואשה), so שחיטה needs its own פסוק.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: when each case has its own stringency, the Torah must write each one separately.

steps.title: What is the source for sprinkling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא has sources for שחיטה and קבלה, and now asks for the source that זריקה must also be לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source for slaughtering and collecting the blood. Where do we learn that sprinkling the blood must also be for the sake of the offering?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next עבודה. It has already shown that שחיטה and קבלה must be לשמה, and now it asks where we learn this for זריקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סוגיא is going through the עבודות one at a time. Two are done: שחיטה (from the earlier source) and קבלה (from ״הַמַּקְרִיב אֶת דַּם הַשְּׁלָמִים״). This question opens the search for זריקה.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found (a source)
Sprinkling or tossing the blood on the מזבח
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: We have found slaughter and collection;
from where do we know sprinkling?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After proving the rule for שחיטה and קבלה, the גמרא moves to the next עבודה, זריקה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that זריקה must be done לשמה.

steps.title: Sprinkling cannot be learned from slaughter and collection
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests learning זריקה from שחיטה and קבלה, then rejects it: those two need the north side of the courtyard and are also done for the inner חטאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: let us learn sprinkling from these two. That does not work, because these two are special. They must be done in the north, and they are also done for the inner sin offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible answer, to learn זריקה from שחיטה and קבלה, and knocks it down right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rule can only be learned from a case that is not stricter. שחיטה and קבלה have two strict points that זריקה does not have. They must be done in the צפון of the courtyard by קדשי קדשים, and they are part of the inner חטאות. Since they are 'stronger,' maybe only they need לשמה.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (a suggestion that will be rejected)
Let us learn (one case from another)
The north side of the עזרה, required for קדשי קדשים
Inner חטאות, whose blood is brought inside the היכל

steps.confusionAlert: The inner חטאות do have a sprinkling, but it is done inside, not on the outer מזבח. So שחיטה and קבלה appear in these offerings, while the sprinkling being discussed here does not.

phrases.english: And if you will say: let us learn from these,
what about these, that they require the north,
phrases.notes: With the holiest offerings, slaughtering and collecting the blood must happen on the north side of the courtyard. Sprinkling has no such rule.

phrases.english: and they are present in the inner sin offerings!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא לֵילַף מֵהָנֵי – מָה לְהָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A suggested answer to step 11, rejected in the same breath.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning זריקה from שחיטה and קבלה together.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שחיטה and קבלה have strict points that זריקה lacks: they need צפון, and they are part of the inner חטאות.

steps.title: A verse teaches sprinkling for the sake of the offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings ״הַזּוֹרֵק אֶת דַּם הַשְּׁלָמִים״ to teach that זריקה must be done for the sake of שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the verse says: 'Who sprinkles the blood of the peace offering.' This teaches that the sprinkling must be for the sake of a peace offering.
steps.whatsHappening: Since learning from the other עבודות failed, the גמרא brings a separate פסוק just for זריקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works the same way as the source for קבלה. The פסוק connects the act of sprinkling to 'the blood of the שלמים,' which shows that the sprinkling must be done with the שלמים in mind.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (we take a different approach)
For the sake of

phrases.english: Rather, the verse says:
"Who sprinkles the blood of the peace offering"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:14

phrases.english: that the sprinkling must be for the sake of a peace offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר קְרָא: ״הַזּוֹרֵק אֶת דַּם הַשְּׁלָמִים״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the suggested derivation is rejected, the גמרא gives a פסוק-based source instead.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק ״הַזּוֹרֵק אֶת דַּם הַשְּׁלָמִים״ teaches that זריקה must be לשמה.
steps.whatToRemember: Each עבודה gets its own source: שחיטה, then קבלה (״הַמַּקְרִיב״), then זריקה (״הַזּוֹרֵק״), because each one is too different to learn from the others.

steps.title: Why not write it only for sprinkling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the Torah did not write the לשמה rule only by זריקה and let us learn the other עבודות from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the Torah write this rule only for sprinkling, and we would learn the other services from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the need for so many פסוקים. Maybe one פסוק about זריקה would have been enough, and the other עבודות could be learned from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of question asked in step 9 about קבלה. If זריקה has no strict point that the others lack, we could learn them from it, and the separate sources for שחיטה and קבלה would seem extra. The answer comes next: the גמרא will show that זריקה has a strict point of its own.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One (the Torah)
And we would learn from it

phrases.english: And let the Merciful One write it about sprinkling,
and we would learn from it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for separate פסוקים, now that זריקה has its own source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for separate פסוקים for שחיטה and קבלה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the Torah had written the rule only for זריקה, we could learn the other עבודות from it, so the extra sources seem unneeded.

steps.title: Why we could not learn everything from זריקה alone
steps.stepSummary: We cannot learn the other עבודות from זריקה, because זריקה is stricter: a זר who does it is punished with מיתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because there is a way to knock down that comparison: what is special about זריקה is that a non-כהן who does it is liable to death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 14. It explains why the Torah had to write לשמה separately for the other עבודות and not only by זריקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rule learned from a stricter case does not automatically carry over to a milder case. זריקה is stricter, because a זר who does it gets מיתה בידי שמים, and that is not true of שחיטה or קבלה. So the לשמה rule of זריקה could not have taught us about them.

keyTerms.meaning: to knock down a comparison by showing that the source case is stricter
a non-כהן
death (here, death by the hand of Heaven)

phrases.english: Because there is room to refute it:
What is special about sprinkling?
That a non-priest is liable to death for doing it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: פירכא: the source case is stricter
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Writing לשמה by זריקה alone would have been enough to teach all the עבודות.

steps.title: What is the source for carrying the blood?

steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's rule of לשמה covers all four blood עבודות. So far, sources were found only for שחיטה, קבלה and זריקה, so הולכה still needs a source.

steps.title: Learning carrying from the other three does not work
steps.stepSummary: Someone might suggest learning הולכה from the other three עבודות. That fails, because they can never be skipped, while הולכה sometimes can.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: let us learn it from all of them. But what is special about all of them is that each is an עבודה that can never be left out. Can you then say the same for הולכה, which can be left out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises the idea of learning הולכה from the other three עבודות together, and then knocks that idea down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שחיטה, קבלה and זריקה must happen in every קרבן. הולכה does not always happen, because if the animal is slaughtered right next to the מזבח, there is no carrying at all. Something that can be skipped cannot simply copy the rules of things that can never be skipped.

steps.title: Carrying is included in receiving the blood
steps.stepSummary: The Torah describes קבלה with the word for bringing close, ״וְהִקְרִיבוּ״. This teaches that הולכה is part of קבלה and follows its rules, including לשמה.

A ברייתא teaches that ״וְהִקְרִיבוּ״ refers to receiving the blood. So the Torah described receiving the blood with a word that means carrying, to teach that carrying is not separate from receiving.

steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new question. It already has a source that an offering must be brought for its own type, and now it wants a source that it must be brought for its own owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of "wrong intention": thinking of a different kind of offering, and thinking of a different person as the owner. Everything up to now covered only the first kind. This question opens the search for the second kind.

steps.title: רב פנחס learns the owner rule from the פסוק about תודה
steps.stepSummary: רב פנחס בריה דרב אמי says the פסוק ״וּבְשַׂר זֶבַח תּוֹדַת שְׁלָמָיו״ is not needed for offering type, so it teaches the owner rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פנחס son of רב אמי said: The פסוק says "And the meat of the sacrifice of his thanksgiving peace offering," meaning the slaughter must be for the sake of a תודה. But we already know the type rule from another place. So use this פסוק for the owner rule.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פנחס answers the question with a פסוק about the תודה. Since we already know the offering-type rule from elsewhere, he says this פסוק must be teaching the owner rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the פסוק says to slaughter for the sake of a תודה, which is the offering-type rule. That rule already has a source, so the פסוק would be extra. Using the method "אם אינו ענין," an extra פסוק is moved over to teach a different rule, here שינוי בעלים.

steps.title: That פסוק is already used by a ברייתא for a different rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: a ברייתא uses the same פסוק to teach that a תודה slaughtered as a שלמים is fit, but not the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: But is this פסוק really here for that? It is needed for what a ברייתא teaches: אבא חנין says in the name of רבי אליעזר that a תודה slaughtered for the sake of a שלמים is fit, but a שלמים slaughtered for the sake of a תודה is unfit. Why the difference? A תודה is called a שלמים, but a שלמים is not called a תודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פנחס. It says the פסוק is not extra at all, because a ברייתא already uses it for another lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פנחס's proof depended on the פסוק being free. The ברייתא shows the פסוק calls the תודה "שְׁלָמָיו," which teaches that a תודה counts as a kind of שלמים. If the פסוק is busy teaching that, it seems it cannot also be moved over to teach the owner rule.

steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 22, רב פנחס learned the owner rule from the extra word ״זֶבַח״. Now the גמרא points out that this word is not really extra. It is already used to teach that חטאת and אשם may only be eaten for one day and a night, like a תודה. A word that is already used for one lesson cannot simply be taken for another.

steps.title: The word's position teaches two lessons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that if ״זֶבַח″ only came to teach about חטאת and אשם, the Torah would have placed it after the phrase. Its placement first shows it teaches both lessons.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the verse write: "And the meat of his thanksgiving peace offering, sacrifice." Why does it say "sacrifice" first? Learn two lessons from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב פנחס. It says the unusual position of the word ״זֶבַח״ lets it teach two lessons at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To teach the eating time of חטאת and אשם, the word ״זֶבַח״ could have been placed at the end of the phrase. Since the Torah puts it first, before ״תּוֹדַת שְׁלָמָיו״, there is an extra hint. So we learn both the eating-time rule and the owner rule (שינוי בעלים).

steps.title: What about the other services?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now has a source that שחיטה must be done for the owner, and asks for the source for the other עבודות.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source for slaughter. From where do we know it for the other services?

steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק of ״זֶבַח״ speaks about slaughter. That only proves the owner rule for שחיטה. The גמרא now needs a source for the other עבודות: קבלה, הולכה, and זריקה.

steps.title: We cannot simply learn from slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects learning the other עבודות from שחיטה, since שחיטה has a special stringency: in a קרבן פסח, slaughtering not for the sake of its eaters disqualifies it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: let us learn from slaughter. But slaughter is special, because in a קרבן פסח, slaughtering not for the sake of the people who will eat it disqualifies it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests an easy answer, learning from שחיטה, and pushes it away right away. This sets up the need for a different source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You cannot copy a rule from a case that is stricter than the case you want to learn. שחיטה is stricter, because in a קרבן פסח it is ruined if done not for the sake of those who will eat it. The other services do not have this rule, so maybe they are also not strict about the owner.

steps.title: Learning the other rites from the matching word 'slaughter'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the question about the other עבודות with a גזירה שוה. The word זביחה is used for both שינוי קודש and שינוי בעלים. Since שינוי קודש covers all four עבודות, שינוי בעלים should cover all four as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'slaughter' is used about changing the type of offering, and the word 'slaughter' is also used about changing the owner. When changing the type of offering, you did not treat slaughter differently from the other rites. So too, when changing the owner, do not treat slaughter differently from the other rites.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new source showing that all the עבודות, not just שחיטה, must be done for the sake of the owner. It links the owner rule to the rule about the type of offering through a shared word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 26, learning straight from שחיטה failed because שחיטה has a special stringency. Now the גמרא learns from a different topic, שינוי קודש, where we already know all four עבודות count. The shared word זביחה lets the full rule carry over to שינוי בעלים.

steps.title: Four ways that changing the type of offering is more severe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא refutes the גזירה שוה. שינוי קודש is more severe than שינוי בעלים in four ways, so its rule cannot simply be carried over to the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: This can be refuted. What is special about changing the type of offering? Its problem is in the offering itself. It applies to all four rites. It applies even after the owner has died. And it applies to communal offerings just as to individual ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the source it just gave. It shows that שינוי קודש is a stronger kind of problem than שינוי בעלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A comparison only works if the two topics are equal. Here the גמרא lists four stringencies of שינוי קודש: the problem touches the offering's own identity, it clearly covers all four עבודות, it still applies after the owner dies, and it applies to public offerings too. Since שינוי בעלים may lack these features, the rule about all four rites cannot be borrowed from שינוי קודש.

steps.whatToRemember: The גזירה שוה from שינוי קודש fails because שינוי קודש is stricter in four ways, so the גמרא still needs a source for the other עבודות in שינוי בעלים.

phrases.english: This can be refuted:
What is special about changing the type of offering?
That its disqualification is in the offering itself,
phrases.notes: He means the wrong intent changes what the offering is, not just whom it is for.

phrases.english: and it applies to all four rites,
and it applies after the owner's death,
and it applies to the community as to an individual!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step refutes the גזירה שוה offered in step 27.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison from שינוי קודש to שינוי בעלים as a source for the other עבודות.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שינוי קודש has four stringencies that שינוי בעלים may not share: the problem is in the offering itself, it covers all four rites, it applies after death, and it applies to communal offerings.
